claims.claim: Camtek's operating-margin compression predates completion of the Visual Layer acquisition: Q1 2026 GAAP operating margin was 22.4% versus 27.6% a year earlier, and non-GAAP operating margin was 25.5% versus 31.5%, while revenue increased only 2.5%. This makes it unsafe to attribute the later Q2 margin compression solely to acquisition accounting or integration costs.
claims.use: Alpha risk-source support; distinguish demand momentum from operating-leverage and cost-base risk without setting a numeric risk score.

claims.claim: Q1 2026 operating cash flow was $3.1 million versus $31.6 million GAAP net income, while Q2 operating cash flow improved to $12.2 million alongside $23.3 million GAAP net income. The two-quarter pattern supports treating cash conversion and margin normalization as evidence questions even as order momentum strengthens.
claims.use: Alpha can source-address financialOperatingMomentum/risk evidence; the observation is not itself a blocker or score.

risks.risk: Operating-margin compression was already visible before the Visual Layer acquisition closed, so sustainable cost leverage remains a live execution question despite strong advanced-packaging demand.

Quarterly operating cash flow has lagged GAAP net income in both Q1 and Q2 2026; working-capital and cash-conversion durability should be reconciled by Alpha using the underlying filings before high financial-confidence treatment.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid order acceleration and improving revenue guidance coexist with pre-acquisition operating-margin compression and comparatively weak operating cash conversion.
contradictions.disposition: clarified_not_resolved: acquisition effects cannot fully explain the margin pattern; Alpha should quantify recurring versus temporary cost/cash-conversion drivers from source-addressed filings.

unknowns.unknown: The share of 2026 margin compression attributable to recurring R&D/SG&A expansion, acquisition-related amortization/integration, mix, or other items is not established by these earnings releases alone.

improvementPath: Alpha should use Q1/Q2 2026 filing-level operating expense, amortization, working-capital and cash-flow line items to separate recurring cost-base pressure from temporary acquisition/integration effects and construct its own numeric risk evidence.
falsifier: If filing-level reconciliation shows the margin and cash-conversion gap is predominantly temporary/non-recurring while recurring operating leverage improves as H2 revenue scales, this risk interpretation should be reduced.
